ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, United Kingdom Sanctions List, South African FIC targeted financial sanctions list, and the SA terrorist and related activities list under s.28A of the FIC Act. PEP status is determined using the FIC Directive on beneficial ownership and PEPs; positive matches or PEP status trigger enhanced due diligence and possible approval by the Accountable Institution's AML Compliance Officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services name reservation module (www.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be in one of the 11 official languages of South Africa, expressed in Latin alphabet characters; if the name is in a language other than English, a transliteration or English translation must be filed with CIPC. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or trademark, and must not imply a false relationship with a person, state, institution, or government.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, CIPC issues a notice citing statutory objections. The applicant, within 30 days of the notice, may file an objection to the Companies Tribunal under s.160 of the Companies Act, 2008, requesting review of the refusal. The applicant may also re-file a fresh name reservation request; an approved reservation may be extended by filing a renewal request before expiry via the CIPC e-Services portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible for the statutory registered office. South African law, specifically s.23(3) of the Companies Act, requires a physical registered office address located in South Africa. A virtual office may be used for operational correspondence, but not as the registered address for service of process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; estimated 15% annual risk of unannounced inspection by CIPC or the Financial Intelligence Centre for this low-risk digital services industry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 13 (registration), 19 (consequences of incorporation), 32 (registered office), 40 (consideration for shares), and 66 (board of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a juristic authority under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) and certificate of incorporation issued by CIPC
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company; at least one shareholder and one director are required. Payment for shares may be cash, future services, or property, subject to the MOI and section 40 of the Companies Act; no escrow account requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscribers, as reflected in the Memorandum of Incorporation, hereby subscribe for the founding shares of the company, and the director is authorised to receive payment or approve consideration for such shares in accordance with section 40 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. 2. The registered office of the company is established at the address stated in the Notice of Incorporation, and all official notices and process may be served there. 3. The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Director and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Financial Director, and [Name] as Company Secretary. 4. These officers are authorised individually to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and perform all acts necessary to commence and carry out the company's business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Login to the CIPC eServices portal, use the company name search tool to check the proposed name against the names database, and file Form CoR 9.1 for name reservation if a desirable name is identified. The application must be completed using the founder's identity number and contact details.
required_dossiers: Proof of applicant's residential or business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict or objection, file a revised name reservation within 10 business days or proceed using the company registration number as the corporate name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting MOI and Internal Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding director(s) and/or legal adviser, with subsequent submission to CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation including share capital structure, director appointment provisions, quorum rules, and any pre-emptive rights. Prepare director consent forms and the registered office notice. Ensure all documents are executed by the founding subscribers.
required_dossiers: Notice of Registered Office and Postal Address (Form CoR 11.1)
Consent to Accept Appointment as Director (Form CoR 14.3 or equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If drafting is incomplete, CIPC will submit a compliance inquiry; correct the deficiencies and resubmit the amended MOI within the prescribed response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed Form CoR 14.1, MOI, and supporting notices through the CIPC eServices interface. Pay the prescribed registration fee using the CIPC accepted payment methods. Upon approval, the CIPC will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and assigned company registration number.
required_dossiers: Consent to Accept Appointment as Director (CoR 14.3)
Certified identity documents of founding directors and subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, review the CIPC rejection reason, correct the affected forms, and resubmit via the same portal within 20 business days to avoid additional registration requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Domestic Compliance Registration with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), branches and eFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a taxpayer reference number for income tax using the Certificate of Incorporation and director details. Assess whether VAT registration is mandatory over the R1 million compulsory turnover threshold; if voluntary VAT registration is desired, submit Form VAT 101. If employees are hired, register for PAYE, UIF, and SDL.
required_dossiers: Proof of principal bank account and physical registered office address
SARS business registration forms (ITREG, VAT 101, EMP101 as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects the registration due to unverifiable details, liaise with the SARS branch to resolve the verification issue, resubmit corrected documents, and request an official taxpayer registration confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational Compliance, Banking, and Employment Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (Compensation Fund), local municipal authority, and commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the Compensation Fund under COIDA using Worksheet WAs/2 and WAs/8. Obtain a municipal business/trading license if the physical premises require one under local zoning bylaws. Open a corporate business bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, and director resolutions. If directors are also payroll earners, finalise UIF registration.
required_dossiers: Registered office and rental agreement or ownership title
Director identification and proof of residential address
Commercial bank account application forms and initial deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the Compensation Fund or municipal authority issue a deficiency notice, provide the outstanding payroll declarations, floor plans, or fire certificates within the stated deadline; for banking, resubmit with supplementary director verification documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 7310 (Advertising Agencies / SEO-Localization Agency) is a non-licensed professional service activity without industrial or manufacturing permits under South African law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence required; however a municipal business/trading licence may be required for physical branch premises depending on local zoning bylaws.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Affairs (Western Cape and Gauteng provincial departments as applicable)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no listed environmental activity under GN R983/984/985 of 4 December 2014 for office-based administrative and digital marketing services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – office premises generate only domestic-type general waste. Any e-waste disposal must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 and municipal waste management bylaws; no wastewater or VOC emissions are generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993: mandatory fire safety certificate from the local Fire Protection Services, structural load confirmation for the leased office, and registration with the Compensation Fund for occupational injury cover. If separate warehousing or hardware staging facilities are used, additional occupational health and structural inspections may be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; principal website https://www.sars.gov.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A South African (Pty) Ltd is registered with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), and SARS automatically links the CIPC registration to obtain an income tax reference number. Foreign branch or non-resident taxpayers must register with SARS via eFiling, providing incorporation/foreign registration documents, an appointed local representative, and a physical South African address. VAT registration is obtained separately through SARS eFiling using the VAT 101 (vendors) or applicable non-resident electronic services registration channel; the compulsory threshold is taxable supplies exceeding ZAR 1,000,000 in a consecutive 12-month period, with voluntary registration available where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in the previous 12 months.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A South African registered (Pty) Ltd is a tax resident and a separate taxable 'person'; no pass-through is available. It is taxed at the corporate rate on worldwide income. A foreign-owned subsidiary similarly has no pass-through status; a foreign company branch is taxed on South African-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists under South African law. Entity classification is fully statutory. Available elections include VAT grouping for closely connected companies under Section 50 of the Value-Added Tax Act and certain filing exception elections; hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory and cannot be bypassed by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 compulsory threshold over any consecutive 12-month period; ZAR 50,000 voluntary registration threshold for resident vendors; non-resident electronic services suppliers are subject to separate SARS registration requirements under the VAT Act electronic services provisions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently operate a real-time e-invoicing clearance or digital stamping mandate. VAT-compliant invoices must meet SARS section 20 requirements, including full vendor name, VAT registration number, invoice date, description, quantity, unit price, and VAT amount. Invoices may be issued electronically, and VAT returns are filed online through SARS eFiling, with electronic data submissions; no separate government clearance API or fiscal stamp is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export goods zero-rated if supplied to a non-resident and removed from South Africa within the prescribed timeframe, with proper documentary proof of export. Export services zero-rated under Section 11(2) of the VAT Act where the services are supplied to a non-resident who is not in South Africa at the time of supply, provided the services are not directly connected with South African land or moveable property retained in South Africa; the services must be performed outside South Africa or supplied for export use, subject to SARS conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) or digital SARS Customs declaration evidencing physical export clearance
Commercial invoice and export/import contract (if applicable), including IRS or client-specific service agreement for zero-rated services
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / carrier or freight-forwarder proof of removal from South Africa for goods; for services, signed affidavit or service performance evidence outside South Africa
Bank or authorised-dealer Inward/Outward Remittance Certificate, foreign currency receipt proof, or SWIFT/electronic transfer evidence showing overseas customer payment in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may deny zero-rating retroactively if the statutory proof-of-export or service-export requirements are not fully maintained. Assessments can be reopened for up to five years (and longer in cases of fraud or non-disclosure). Understatement penalties under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 range from 10% to 200% of the shortfall, with additional interest charges. Wilful fraudulent zero-rating claims attract criminal liability, fines, possible imprisonment, and statutory additional tax including full repayment of VAT previously credited or refunded.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), under the Currency and Exchanges Act, No. 9 of 1933, and the Exchange Control Rulings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is a free-floating, fully convertible currency for current-account transactions, including export of services and profit/dividend remittances by non-resident shareholders, subject to normal authorised-dealer reporting and SARS tax-clearance verification. Capital-account transactions such as inbound equity subscriptions and shareholder loans require SARB FinSurv compliance via an authorised dealer, but no broad convertibility blockage exists for a legitimate services exporter. Profit remittance is permitted on proof of taxed profits, withholding tax compliance, and standard Anti-Money Laundering/Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) checks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: 100% of service export proceeds (including ASO/SEO localization fees) must be repatriated to South Africa through an authorised dealer within 180 days after the service completion date or invoice date. No fixed statutory conversion ratio into ZAR is imposed; the exporter may credit proceeds to a SARB-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) maintained with an authorised dealer, and any conversion to ZAR must occur at the prevailing arm's-length market rate. Late repatriation or failure to surrender constitutes an exchange-control offence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
First National Bank (FNB, a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (with integrated FX and electronic banking)
Operational Account and dedicated Trade/Forward Book
Capital Escrow Account / Premium Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium as a supplementary collection rail, but not as primary treasury infrastructure. Wise B2B and Payoneer are non-bank payment facilitators and are not SARB-licensed authorised dealers. They may be used for low-value onboarding of clients via card/ACH, but all export proceeds must ultimately be routed into a South African authorised-dealer banking relationship within the 180-day surrender window. Holding funds in such EMIs for extended periods could be treated as unauthorised offshore accounts; therefore, a weekly or bi-monthly sweep to the local operational account is mandatory under a prudent treasury policy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is possible for standard-risk corporate clients using real-time FICA verification, biometric checks, and video KYC under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act; however, for a newly incorporated non-resident-held (Pty) Ltd with no established local footprint, the majority of tier-1 banks require at least one authorised director or signatory to attend a physical interview at a South African branch or to complete a notarised interview before a bank-designated officer. Where all directors are non-residents, a physical visit or a combination of remote video verification plus courier-notarised corporate documents is the prevailing standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% foreign beneficial ownership of a newly formed South African (Pty) Ltd with no South African directors and no substantial fixed-asset base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised copy of the CIPC certificate of incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation; share register and beneficial-ownership declaration; valid passports and proof of residence for all ultimate beneficial owners; certified Board Resolution appointing signatories; a registered physical-office lease agreement; company tax clearance certificate; projected cash-flow statement and source-of-wealth documents for the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-marketing agency receiving high-frequency cross-border payments from multiple jurisdictions, including those with elevated AML risk or non-transparent corporate vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service contracts naming each client legal entity; granular commercial invoices describing ASO/SEO deliverables; platform performance reports (App Store Connect, Google Play Console, Google Analytics) that evidence genuine service delivery; completed beneficial-ownership records or company extracts for materially significant clients; internal client risk-rating documentation under the company's risk management and compliance programme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank concern over insufficient economic substance and operating costs inconsistent with revenue volume, suggesting possible round-tripping or money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Management accounts for the current fiscal period; periodic payroll and contractor remittance reports demonstrating local employment; board-approved budget and cash-flow forecast; evidence of dedicated office infrastructure; paid-to-date SARS tax compliance records; external accountant's independent review where material; a written treasury memo documenting the business rationale for the volume of invoice traffic and sub-contractor flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident equity capital must be introduced via a SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's own banking relationship, referencing the share subscription agreement and using the bank's prescribed inward investment purpose code (typically 'EQUITY CAPITAL' or 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION'). The local authorised dealer will log the inward transfer, issue a foreign-exchange conversion certificate where the funds are converted to ZAR, and create an SARB-control reference number for the facility. All inward remittance documents, including the bank's 'Inward Notification' letter and the capital-account schedule, must be retained for compliance reviews and future dividend-repatriation justification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Service-related disbursements to foreign subcontractors, freelancers, and technology vendors should be executed by SWIFT MT103 wires routed through the company's authorised dealer, supported by the underlying invoice, approved purchase order, and internal treasury authorisation in accordance with the four-eyes principle. For large, time-certain transactions, the company may utilise a commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) through its trade-finance desk; however, given the intangible-services nature of ASO/SEO operations, MT103s with full supporting documentation are the primary clearing rail. All foreign-currency purchases must be transacted on a deliverable basis via the local bank, and no payments may be made to sanctioned jurisdictions without explicit FinSurv and OFAC-comparative screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) with a SARB-authorized dealer for hedging fixed ZAR/USD or ZAR/EUR receivable/payable flows arising from service contracts.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for economically hedging the interest and principal on long-term shareholder loans or intercompany funding.
Plain-vanilla FX options, including zero-cost collars, used to protect profit margins on non-ZAR invoice cash flows.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for onshore resident entities without an express FinSurv approval; therefore, treasury policy should rely exclusively on deliverable instruments transacted with local authorised dealers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (CIPC Form AR) — corporate renewal declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation/registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company flagged as 'delinquent' and certificate of good standing withheld; late-filing charges apply; continued non-filing for two or more consecutive years exposes the company to administrative deregistration (strike-off) by CIPC under s82 of Companies Act 71 of 2008 and director disqualification proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (BO) Declaration — annual confirmation of members and ultimate beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the Annual Return (within 30 business days of incorporation anniversary); shareholding transfers or BO changes must be declared within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false declaration is a criminal offence under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022, punishable by fines up to ZAR 10 million or imprisonment up to 10 years; CIPC flags the company as non-compliant and may refuse transactional authorisations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) with statutory audit report or independent review report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Prepared for shareholders and retained at the registered office; CIPC filing mandated only when the Public Interest Score is 500 or more
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors must prepare AFS within 6 months after financial year-end; where audit/review is triggered, the report must be tabled and shareholders notified within the same 6-month period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability for non-compliance with ss29–30 of Companies Act 71 of 2008; CIPC enforcement notices and administrative monetary penalties for contravention; failure to appoint a registered auditor where required is a separate administrative offence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and annual provisional tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: ITR14 due within 12 months of financial year-end; provisional tax estimate filings due at the 6-month and 12-month points of the tax year with the final top-up payment due within 6 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty up to ZAR 8,000 per month for late or non-submission; interest at the SARS prescribed rate on outstanding amounts; underpayment penalty of up to 20% on provisional tax shortfalls where estimates fall below the statutory thresholds; SARS may block tax clearance certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where the company's Public Interest Score (PIS) is 500 or more; PIS 350–499 requires an independent review by a registered accountant unless the MOI or shareholders resolve for a full audit; PIS below 350 requires no audit or review unless the MOI or a shareholder resolution compels one, but annual financial statements must still be prepared.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs in accordance with Companies Act 71 of 2008 s29; full IFRS is compulsory for companies with a Public Interest Score of 500 or more, while IFRS for SMEs is permitted for lower-scored eligible private companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Annual Return must be accompanied by a Beneficial Ownership (BO) declaration confirming the current register of members, shareholding proportions, and ultimate beneficial owners. Any shareholding transfer must be recorded in the securities register and, where the transfer changes beneficial ownership, declared to CIPC within 30 days of the transaction; the on-site BO register and Annual Return must also be updated accordingly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 80–250 per annum for a registered office address and CIPC company secretarial/registered-agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not compulsory at PIS below 350; optional full statutory audit USD 3,000–8,000, or independent review USD 1,500–3,500 if PIS 350–499
